customer_question: Can we use the BQBTestUtilityM tool instead of testing through the product's own user interface, and does that affect the validity of the resulting report? Also, since the tool doesn't make the product actually output audio, is confirming via its Log Message enough for audio-related test items?
question_variants: Does using a Profile Test Application tool make our PTS report less valid as evidence?
Will it be obvious from the report that we used BQBTestUtilityM instead of the real product interface?
How do we handle PTS test items that ask us to confirm audio output if the tool doesn't actually play audio?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to use a Profile Test Application tool (BQBTestUtilityM) running on Linux against PTS, instead of setting up each test's Initial Condition through the product's own user interface, and separately raised that this tool does not cause the product to actually output audio, requiring clarification on whether the tool's Log Message could substitute for audio-output confirmation in the relevant PTS test items, and whether either of these affected the registration evidence's validity.
plain_english_explanation: Setting up a Bluetooth test condition by hand through a product's actual buttons and menus for every single test item takes a lot of time. A specialized testing utility can do this setup automatically instead, which speeds things up a lot -- and importantly, the official test report that comes out the other end looks exactly the same either way, so using the utility doesn't create any visible difference or weaken the evidence. The one wrinkle is that for tests that specifically ask a human to confirm whether audio actually played, the utility itself doesn't make sound come out of the device, so that confirmation step has to rely on the company's own separate, prior confirmation that audio works correctly with a real paired device, rather than something heard during this specific test run.
consultant_answer: BQBTestUtilityM is a Profile Test Application that runs on Linux and tests against PTS, following a documented procedure (referenced from an earlier reply). In principle, profile testing should use the product's own FW/SW/User Interface, but testing based on this tool saves the effort of setting up each test's Initial Condition through the product's own user interface, making testing more efficient. The resulting PTS report carries no record of BQBTestUtilityM having been used, so it is identical to a report from testing the actual product directly, and can be used without issue as registration evidence. Recommend proceeding with BQBTestUtilityM-based testing. Separately, for the audio-output confirmation question: PTS test items requiring audio-output confirmation cannot be judged automatically by PTS -- they require a human to manually press the confirm button on a confirmation-request dialog. Since BQBTestUtilityM does not cause the product to actually output audio, the approach taken is to press the confirm button on the premise that the applicant has already separately confirmed audio output works correctly when paired with a real device. As a result, the PTS report's record does not automatically capture whether audio output occurred, so this approach does not affect the validity of the report's content.
decision_logic: A Profile Test Application tool that replaces direct product-interface testing to save Initial Condition setup effort does not affect the validity of the resulting PTS report as registration evidence, since the report carries no record of which method was used. For audio-output confirmation test items that the tool cannot itself produce, manually confirming the dialog on the premise of separately-verified real-device audio behavior does not compromise report validity, since PTS does not automatically capture audio-output presence as part of its report regardless of testing method.
final_recommendation: Approve the use of a Profile Test Application tool like BQBTestUtilityM in place of direct product-interface testing, since the resulting PTS report is evidentially identical either way. For audio-output confirmation steps the tool cannot itself produce, proceed with manual dialog confirmation based on the applicant's own prior verification of real-device audio behavior.
risk_if_done_wrong: Refusing to use a Profile Test Application tool out of concern it would weaken the registration evidence would add unnecessary testing complexity and time without any actual evidentiary benefit, since the resulting report is identical either way.
